---
title: Contribute a Reproducible Learning Lab
description: Turn a planned lesson into reviewed instruction without weakening its checks.
---

## 1. Choose one planned outcome

Use the tracked catalog, unit overview, and outcome map to find the owning unit,
stable lesson ID, intended scope, and expected learner evidence. All `PLAN*.md`
files are ignored local material, not prerequisites for contributing, running
tests, or building the site. If a maintainer supplies a local `PLAN-LESSONS.md`,
also use its detailed teaching brief and lab checks. Keep the current task
narrower than its unit outcome. Do not turn all 101 outlines into thin published
pages.

When using that local tracker, maintain the task's development status, owner,
date, blockers, and evidence. Explicitly run `poetry run makim plan.refresh` and
`poetry run makim plan.check` after updates. These commands need the local plan;
CI and normal pytest runs do not read it. CI tests the validator using synthetic
records and checks public curriculum relationships using tracked sources.
A finished brief is not an implemented lesson; unit gates and capstone stages
are tracked separately. Development state does not replace catalog publication
state or imply verified learner completion.

The source layout keeps QMD under `docs/courses/agentic-ai-engineering/`, reusable
Python under `src/freecampus_agents/`, and tests under `tests/`. This adapts the draft
plan's illustrative nested layout to the existing repository's package structure.

## 2. Make the task runnable without a paid provider

Supply synthetic or openly licensed fixtures, a deterministic fake boundary, and
machine-checkable ordinary and failure cases. Keep tool permissions and budgets
explicit. Record observable events and concise rationales, not private reasoning.
Never redistribute secrets, private data, or unlicensed recorded responses.

## 3. Author the lesson, not just its summary

Include a concrete task, 3–5 opening questions, a measurable outcome, active-time
estimate, explanations, predictions, controlled changes, and debugging practice.
Use three small checkpoints for concept, evidence, and failure diagnosis; give
plausible distractors and explanations. Finish with a checked lab and primary
references. Overviews stay quiz-free; planned project outlines are not assessments.

Unit challenges take 90–180 minutes and include a contract, progressive checks,
three hint levels, injected failures, a hidden solution, and an evidence record.
The templates are scaffolds outside the rendered course, not publishable lessons.

## 4. Keep publication records synchronized

When a lesson is genuinely available, update its catalog status, front matter,
course progress IDs, available counts, outcome map, and sidebar together. Add the
Colab include and a unique notebook path. Never link a planned path that does not
exist. Do not enable whole-course completion until the completion contract is ready.

## 5. Check from a clean environment

Use Poetry 2.4+ within the 2.x series. The migration could not connect to PyPI,
so `poetry.lock` has not been generated. Run `poetry lock` with registry access,
inspect and version the result, and add `poetry check --lock --strict` before CI
installation. Until that step, dependency resolution is not pinned transitively.
Do not describe the scaffold as a fully reproducible release or reuse another
course's lockfile.

Conda + Poetry are required locally and in CI. `conda.yaml` supplies Python 3.12,
Poetry, Node.js, and pip. Poetry installs project dependencies directly into the
activated Conda environment. The shared `poetry.toml` disables separate virtual
environments; the environment check rejects nested venvs or mismatched tools.
Use `poetry install`, not synchronization, to preserve Conda-owned tooling.
Activate the environment in each terminal and select its Python in your editor.
Pre-commit hooks use these installed tools rather than creating hook environments.

```bash
conda env create -f conda.yaml  # First setup only
conda activate fc-agentic
python scripts/check_environment.py
poetry check --strict
poetry install --all-extras --with docs
python scripts/check_environment.py
poetry run pytest -q
poetry run ruff check src tests scripts
poetry run ruff format --check src tests scripts
poetry run mypy src
poetry build
poetry run makim docs.build
git diff --check
poetry run makim clean.tmp
```

The build renders HTML, exports notebooks, and verifies expected output files.
Open at least one desktop and narrow-screen quiz when browser tooling is available.
Restart the smoke notebook and run from the top. Report skipped checks and external
limitations rather than treating unrun checks as passing.

Use the [repository contribution guidance](https://github.com/freecampus/agentic-ai-engineering/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
and [Poetry's basic usage](https://python-poetry.org/docs/basic-usage/) for further detail.
